headline: Portugal coach Roberto Martinez steps down after World Cup exit to Spain
summary: Martinez cited the team's elimination from the World Cup last 16 as the "end of a cycle" and stated his contract expired after the defeat.
details: Portugal manager Roberto Martinez has announced his departure from the role following the team's 1-0 defeat to Spain in the World Cup last 16. He described the loss as the conclusion of a cycle for the national team.
Martinez, whose contract expired on Monday, stated his intention to leave if he didn't win the World Cup. He believes the Portuguese football leadership should now select a new manager.
The Spanish coach expressed immense pride in his time with Portugal, feeling "welcomed as just another Portuguese person." He confirmed the match against Spain was his last in charge.

Martinez also offered a glowing farewell to captain Cristiano Ronaldo, praising him as an "exemplary captain" for his commitment and contributions. Ronaldo's long international career is also expected to conclude.

He reflected on the match, noting that Portugal showed courage and aggression against a tournament favorite. However, he attributed the defeat to "small details" that make all the difference in World Cup knockout stages.
caption:
Portugal coach Roberto Martinez has resigned after the team's World Cup exit to Spain. He stated his contract expired and that not winning the World Cup meant "no point in continuing."

Portugal manager Roberto Martinez has announced his departure from the role following the team's 1-0 defeat to Spain in the World Cup last 16. He described the loss as the conclusion of a cycle for the national team.

Martinez, whose contract expired on Monday, stated his intention to leave if he didn't win the World Cup. He believes the Portuguese football leadership should now select a new manager.

The Spanish coach expressed immense pride in his time with Portugal, feeling "welcomed as just another Portuguese person." He confirmed the match against Spain was his last in charge.

Martinez also offered a glowing farewell to captain Cristiano Ronaldo, praising him as an "exemplary captain" for his commitment and contributions. Ronaldo's long international career is also expected to conclude.

He reflected on the match, noting that Portugal showed courage and aggression against a tournament favorite. However, he attributed the defeat to "small details" that make all the difference in World Cup knockout stages.

headline: Portugal won nothing before Cristiano Ronaldo," star says after World Cup exit
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's World Cup journey ended with Portugal's defeat, prompting him to reflect on his international future and his significant contributions to the national team.
details: Portugal's World Cup campaign concluded with a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the round-of-16, courtesy of Mikel Merino's last-gasp winner. This marked the end of Cristiano Ronaldo's final World Cup appearance.

Ronaldo expressed sadness at leaving the tournament, stating he gave his all and leaves with a clear conscience. He confirmed this was his last World Cup, but will take time to reflect before deciding his international future.

The 41-year-old proudly highlighted his contribution, stating, "I've won three titles for Portugal; before Cristiano Ronaldo, Portugal hadn't won a single title." He helped secure the 2016 European Championship and the Nations League in 2019.

Ronaldo felt the match could have swung either way, attributing Spain's winning goal to "a bit of luck." He also offered warm words for departing manager Roberto Martinez, praising him as a great manager and human being.
caption:

The 41-year-old proudly highlighted his contribution, stating, "I've won three titles for Portugal; before Cristiano Ronaldo, Portugal hadn't won a single title." He helped secure the 2016 European Championship and the Nations League in 2019.

Ronaldo felt the match could have swung either way, attributing Spain's winning goal to "a bit of luck." He also offered warm words for departing manager Roberto Martinez, praising him as a great manager and human being.
